notes:
Summary: Skybound is a regulated digital banking platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing conversational flows and high-throughput document reranking. Primary ask: well-defined latency SLOs and repeatable measurement methodology for streaming and non-streaming workloads before committing reserved GPUs.

Key quotes from execs: "We need p95 under 300ms for single-turn client requests; streaming can be looser if first-byte arrives within 120ms" (Head of Prod). "Show us server+client aligned metrics — we can't buy on server-only clocks" (SRE lead).

Requirements (bulleted, from discovery + tech deep-dive):
- Workloads: live chat (multi-turn streaming), account summarization (non-streaming), legal doc reranking (batch inference).
- Latency targets: p50/p95/p99 goals required per route. Initial targets proposed: chat first-byte p50=80ms, p95=160ms, p99=350ms (streaming first-byte), non-streaming generation end-to-end p50<=120ms, p95<=300ms, p99<=700ms for <=512 tokens.
- Throughput: peak 1k concurrent chat sessions, sustained batch rerank 200 qps during business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; prefer predictable reserved GPU pricing vs burst.
- Security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, audit logs with 1y retention, data residency in us-east-1.
- Measurement alignment: want both client-side and server-side histograms, distributed tracing correlation (trace-id in headers), and Redwood-provided percentiles computed on server and exported raw timing samples for Skybound to recompute.

POC asks from Skybound engineering:
- Redwood to run a 48-hour dedicated capacity POC with workload replay from production traces (anonymized).
- Stress test plan: step up to 1.5x expected peak for 3 rolling windows. Capture p50/p95/p99 for streaming first-byte, streaming last-token latency, non-streaming end-to-end, and GPU utilization.
- Provide SDK snippet for client-side timing (start/first-byte/end) and examples integrating with Skybound's Datadog traces.

Legal/compliance touches: security questionnaire submitted (Drive link). Legal needs SLA on latency availability for dedicated pool; negotiating penalty language for sustained p95 violations over a 1-hour window.

Internal AE notes: keep cadence weekly until SLO signoff. Finance wants firm ARR commit by 2025-03 or they move to second vendor shortlist.

Short choppy items typical of CRM notes:
- 2025-01-12: intro call, product overview, asked for SLO definitions
- 2025-01-28: tech deep-dive (Diego + SRE), sent replay dataset sample
- 2025-02-05: meeting with security & legal (Fireflies ff_2025-02-05_374b)
- 2025-02-18: price anchor shared; Skybound requested POC plan
- 2025-02-20: alignment call on pXX semantics (client vs server), follow-up doc sent

Internal sentiment: high technical fit but rigorous measurement requests. Likely to close if POC demonstrates repeatable p95 < 300ms non-streaming and streaming first-byte guarantees for 99% of sessions.

slo_requirements:
Deliverable: mutually agreed SLO matrix + measurement plan. Proposed SLOs: non-streaming generation: p50<=120ms, p95<=300ms, p99<=700ms (<=512 tokens). Streaming chat: first-byte p50<=80ms, p95<=160ms, p99<=350ms; time-to-last-token measured separately. Measurement alignment: Redwood server timestamps (ingest, queue, model_start, model_end, transmit) AND client-side sdk start/first-byte/end timestamps. Percentiles computed from raw request-level samples; avoid aggregator-only percentiles. Include per-route histograms and export of raw samples for Skybound's audit.
Measurement methodology notes: synthetic vs production replay, stable sampling (1:1 for POC), tracing header (X-Trace-Id), clock sync guidance (NTP + monotonic clocks), document threshold for SLA breach (sustained p95 > target for 1 hour).
